hypothesis: Non-financial HS300 firms that rank strongly within their own industry on management-cost discipline, operating cash-flow conversion and gross-margin improvement should outperform firms whose weakest industry-relative component is weak, while avoiding comparison of accounting ratios across structurally different sectors.
selection_basis: R253's cross-market weakest-link factor passed both IC segments, the discovery relative gate, validation, full-sample and rolling gates but failed the recent-12-month, 4x/5x cost and net-P&L concentration gates. R254 is a separate hypothesis, fixed before reading its forward returns: accounting ratios are more comparable within industries, so each component is ranked against same-date peers in the same current industry. Feasibility shows 100% coverage, 100% recent coverage, and maximum mean absolute correlation 0.379599. Evidence: r254_data_feasibility.json.

factor.formula: industry_management_ocf_gm_min_rank = min(industry_rank_pct(management_expense_ratio_4q_low), industry_rank_pct(ocf_margin_4q), industry_rank_pct(gross_margin_yoy_improvement_q)); each percentile is computed on the same date within one current industry among nonfinancial historical HS300 members, with 1 = best and 0 = worst
factor.singleton_rule: Industries with one eligible stock receive a neutral 0.5 percentile for that component because no within-industry ordering exists.
factor.interpretation: Higher means the firm's weakest industry-relative quality component remains strong versus same-industry peers.
factor.pit_rule: All components inherit their existing financial PIT dates. Membership and industry ranks use only same-date historical membership and the current industry snapshot; no future financial report, future return or full-sample rank is used.
factor.missing_data_rule: Require all three components to be non-null and a nonfinancial industry label. Missing values remain null; no partial score, zero fill, interpolation or cross-industry fallback.
factor.universe: historical HS300 membership excluding banks and non-bank financials using the current industry snapshot

strategies.weight_rationale: The industry-relative min-rank receives the fixed 45% research weight used in recent rounds. The remaining quality and cash weights preserve the 54.5/45.5 ratio of the matched control. No weight was selected using forward returns.
strategies.matched_requirements: Both strategies use the same nonfinancial HS300 universe, three-component availability filter, 30-name score limit, top 10 equal-weight positions, 20-day holding period, -20% stop loss, T+1 open execution and cost model.

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four cost components proportionally

segments.stitching: compound two independently run segment curves; skip the first return of each later segment

factor_ic.method: month-end factor value versus T+1 open to T+21 open forward return within historical non-financial HS300 members; cross-sectional Spearman rank IC

gates.D1: full-period non-financial member-row factor coverage from 2023-05-04 onward >= 0.99
gates.D3: same-date within-industry min-rank construction, singleton neutral rule, component coverage, ties, historical membership and PIT audit pass
gates.D4: maximum mean absolute monthly rank correlation with the preregistered existing-factor set <= 0.70
gates.I1: discovery mean rank IC >= 0.02 with at least 18 month-end observations
gates.I2: validation mean rank IC >= 0.01 with at least 18 month-end observations and the same positive sign
gates.G2: discovery candidate MDD is no worse than control MDD by more than 5pp
gates.G4: full-sample candidate return > 0 and >= control return
gates.G5: full-sample candidate MDD <= 40% in absolute value and no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G6: rolling 1-year positive rate >= 60% and no worse than control by more than 2pp
gates.G7: recent 12-month candidate return > 0 and MDD no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G8: full-sample candidate return at 4x cost is positive
gates.G9: full-sample candidate return at 5x cost is positive
gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full sample
gates.C2: the largest symbol's share of net P&L is <= 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is <= 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is <= 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the largest industry's share of gross profit is <= 45%
gates.C7: the largest single-symbol loss is <= 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All D, I, G and C gates must pass. Any failure means the factor is not accepted and cannot be rescued by changing the industry-rank rule, singleton treatment, management-cost component, weights, holding period, stop loss, universe, costs or gates after seeing results.
known_limitations: The current industry snapshot is not historical PIT.
Some industries contain only one eligible stock and receive neutral 0.5 ranks.
Industry-relative ranks can be noisy in small peer groups.
Average percentile ranks can produce ties.
Management expenses do not capture selling expenses and may be classified inconsistently across firms.
All components use current financial snapshots and inherit restatement risk.
This is another composite built from the same broad quality-factor family, so multiple-comparison risk remains.
Passing these gates would justify further paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
